title: License renewal + SOC2 artifact handoff — Procurement & IT sync
next_steps: Marcus to upload vendor license spreadsheet to procurement drive (link provided) by 2026-10-02
Erin to attach SOC2 scope matrix and KMS architecture diagram to the ticket by 2026-10-05
Priya to draft the procurement clause changes and circulate by 2026-10-06
Liam to confirm budget line for enterprise seats and share PO template by 2026-10-03
action_items: Marcus Li - Upload license inventory CSV + highlight upcoming renewals - due 2026-10-02
Erin Cho - Share SOC2 artifact list and KMS key rotation policy excerpt - due 2026-10-05
Priya Shah - Revise license language for auto-renewal opt-out and send to Carlos - due 2026-10-06
Liam Patel - Validate cost center and add PO reference for Q4 renewal - due 2026-10-03
summary: Internal sync to align procurement, IT ops and security on several upcoming vendor license renewals and to hand off SOC2-related artifacts for external audit prep. Main topics: clarify license seat counts, confirm whether vendor provides audited artifact set, align KMS/HSM documentation, and decide on procurement language for auto-renewal and termination. Agreed owners and due dates for artifact uploads and legal review.
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia Nguyen: Okay good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. We're here to cover the license renewals block and hand off SOC two artifacts to procurement and legal. We got about 50 minutes, so let's run through the spreadsheet and the artifact list.
[00:22] Carlos Martinez: Hey Sofia, can you confirm which vendors are on the Q4 renewal list again? I pulled a quick export but there are a couple of columns missing.
[00:30] Marcus Li: Yeah Carlos, I emailed the raw csv earlier — it's in the procurement drive, folder 'Q4-Renewals-2026'. I'll re-upload the version with the seat counts filled in. Sorry the export omitted the "entitlements" column, that was my bad.
[00:44] Priya Shah: Quick note, legal needs to see the auto-renewal clause and termination notice periods — some of the SaaS vendors default to 60 days which is annoying for finance.
[00:53] Liam Patel: This is the finance ops point — we want a 30-day termination notice where possible, otherwise we need an explicit opt-out clause. Also, if a vendor requires PO terms on renewal, we need their invoice mapping.
[01:10] Erin Cho: From a compliance perspective, for SOC2 audit prep we only need the subset of artifacts that are in-scope. I'll upload the scope matrix and an index of artifacts (logs, config exports, KMS rotation docs). Note some vendor docs reference 'Vault' or 'HSM' but call it provider synonyms — transcription may show as Hashi/hava/vault and we should make sure the architecture diagram is clear.
[01:36] Carlos Martinez: Marcus, can you share the link in chat? I can't find the correct folder.
[01:40] Marcus Li: Sure. Link pasted: drive.redwoodinternal/company/procurement/Q4-Renewals-2026 — I'll also attach the sheet to the meeting notes.
[01:51] Sofia Nguyen: Perfect. Walk me through the top three renewals: 1) Large inference vendor contract (we call them 'InferenceCorp' internal), 2) Identity provider (Okta renewal), 3) Data storage analytics license.
[02:05] Marcus Li: Inference vendor — seat-based and commit tiers. Current count 120 seats, but usage shows 95 active. There's a clause for unused seats credit but it's manual to apply. Renewal notice is 45 days. Okta is a subscription with annual billing and SSO modules — renewal 90 days. Storage analytics is on a committed use plan through GCP.
[02:29] Priya Shah: On Inference vendor: legal flagged the indemnity and data processing addendum. We need their data retention and deletion policy for our privacy exhibit. If they host logs, we need to know retention windows for the S3 buckets and if retention is adjustable per customer.
[02:45] Erin Cho: Right — specifically for SOC2 we need proof of retention config and who has access to keys. Do they use customer-managed keys or vendor-managed? If vendor-managed, we need the vendor's KMS diagrams and key rotation policies.
[02:58] Marcus Li: I have a vendor note that says 'supports Bring Your Own Key via AWS KMS' — but the doc is ambiguous. I'll flag it as BYOK candidate.
[03:06] Carlos Martinez: Can we make a decision point today about BYOK for the large vendor? The procurement cycle needs to know if we will require BYOK for regulated clients.
[03:14] Sofia Nguyen: I don't think we can decide here — need security and product input. But we can set an action: Erin to request a KMS architecture diagram and confirm whether the vendor supports CMKs.
[03:25] Erin Cho: Yep, I'll add that. Also, I will attach a redacted example of our SOC2 artifact index so vendors can see the naming conventions.
[03:33] Tariq Ahmed: One finance question — if a vendor forces auto-renew with payment in full, can we put a clause to prorate for decommissioned seats mid-term?
[03:40] Priya Shah: We can request prorate language; it's standard. If they refuse, escalate to the vendor management team for negotiation.
[03:48] Sofia Nguyen: Great. Let's go over the artifact handoff process: Marcus uploads inventory; Erin provides the SOC2 matrix; Priya will update template contract language; Liam will confirm budget/PO. Then we reconvene next week for final signoff.
[04:02] Marcus Li: I'll also add a column in the spreadsheet for 'artifact required for SOC2' — true/false, and a doc link.
[04:10] Sofia Nguyen: Good. There's also the matter of the external auditor's checklist — whoever will be coordinating with them needs a canonical set of PDF exports. Erin, can you confirm what exports are acceptable?
[04:20] Erin Cho: Auditors want logs (filter window), config snapshots, evidence of key rotation for the past 12 months, and change control records. I'll prepare a list of exact filenames and acceptable timestamp ranges.
[04:33] Carlos Martinez: On the procurement side, I need the vendor's W9 and bank info to process pre-pay refunds, sometimes they won't accept PO without that. Marcus can you collect those?
[04:40] Marcus Li: Yep, I'll add a 'vendor legal docs' tab.
[04:44] Sofia Nguyen: There was a question from security about whether we can use the vendor's SOC2 report in lieu of certain artifact requests — is that adequate?
[04:52] Erin Cho: Auditor sometimes accepts vendor SOC2 reports but still asks for configuration evidence. So it's a helpful supplement but not a replacement. Also check the SOC2 date range and whether it covers the same control set.
[05:05] Priya Shah: Also watch for third-party subprocessors listed in their report — that can expand our scope. We may need additional attestations.
[05:12] Liam Patel: For finance approvals, we need a consolidated cost per seat and renewal delta year-over-year. Marcus can calculate the delta and show a one-page summary for budget sign-off.
[05:25] Marcus Li: Will do. I'll include a 'delta' column and highlight seats with reductions or expansions.
[05:30] Sofia Nguyen: We also had a vendor that offers an enterprise license with a multi-year discount — is it worth negotiating to lock price given the ML infra growth? Liam?
[05:38] Liam Patel: Depends on forecast. If forecasted consumption increases >20% it's usually cheaper to stay annual because of flexibility, but multi-year gives discount. I'll model 1-, 2-, and 3-year cost scenarios and share in the sheet.
[05:50] Sofia Nguyen: Excellent. Back to SOC2 artifacts: Erin, any issues getting vendor-provided logs? Sometimes vendors only provide aggregated metrics and not raw logs.
[05:58] Erin Cho: True — that is a blocker. We should explicitly request raw access or agreed export APIs. If they can't provide, we need compensating controls (e.g., telemetry via our sidecar).
[06:12] Priya Shah: Please capture that as a risk item — inability to obtain raw logs.
[06:17] Sofia Nguyen: Noted. Next section — identity provider renewal (Okta). Marcus, is it a seat-based renewal or module based?
[06:24] Marcus Li: Module-based. We are renewing SSO + Advanced MFA. Renewal window 90 days. There is an enterprise support add-on we might drop.
[06:33] Carlos Martinez: Support add-on impacts SLA and incident response — let's not drop until we confirm incident response expectations.
[06:40] Erin Cho: From security, we want to keep Advanced MFA. Also confirm federated logging export for user activity for SOC2 evidence.
[06:48] Sofia Nguyen: Good. Any other vendors?
[06:51] Marcus Li: A smaller analytics tool — renewal is auto for committed usage. No SOC2 artifact required.
[06:57] Sofia Nguyen: Ok. Let's move to timeline and owners again.
[07:01] Sofia Nguyen: Recap: Marcus upload CSV + vendor legal docs; Erin share SOC2 artifact index + KMS diagram; Priya revise contract clauses; Liam confirm budget. We'll meet next Thursday for a dry-run of the packet.
[07:16] Tariq Ahmed: Does procurement need a formal sign-off form? We use a PO + two approvers for >$50k.
[07:23] Carlos Martinez: Yes procurement needs the PO template and approver chain. Marcus please add approvers.
[07:28] Marcus Li: Will add.
notes: Meeting was primarily an internal cross-functional alignment; no external vendors on the call.
A shared procurement drive link was referenced and will contain the canonical CSV and artifact uploads.
There was some minor transcription noise around vendor product names (InferenceCorp, Vault/HSM references).
